fact: The New Times quotes a Ministry of Local Government official saying the Imibereho registry is integrated with other government databases, including land records and Rwanda Social Security Board salary data, and records tax paid through the Rwanda Revenue Authority.

BMZ's Healthy DEvelopments says Imibereho data is validated by cross-checks with the National ID Agency, LODA's MEIS and the Health Monitoring Information System, and updates automatically through integration with civil registration, at its launch on 29 February 2024.

BMZ's Healthy DEvelopments says Imibereho initially targets households for the Vision Umurenge Programme and determines payments for community-based health insurance, to extend gradually to other programmes.

BMZ's Healthy DEvelopments says Imibereho is cross-checked with the National ID Agency and the health information system and is integrated with civil registration, so a registered birth updates the registry.
The World Bank says Rwanda's Imibereho Social Registry covers 13.8 million people and supports safety nets, economic inclusion, skills and health insurance programmes.
The World Bank project paper says the Imibereho dynamic social registry integrates data from more than 10 government agencies and interoperates with more than 10 government databases.

The paper's results framework counts systems interlinked to the social registry, from 0 in July 2022 to a target of 10 by December 2028, and the additional financing funds improved interoperability of the registry with other systems and MEIS.

The paper says the share of VUP beneficiaries identified through the dynamic social registry rose from 0 to 100 percent by end-February 2026, and that the registry facilitates access to the Ejo Heza long-term savings scheme and community-based health insurance.

The paper says the Imibereho platform is anchored in the national ID system and interoperates with more than 10 government databases, and that Smart Start targeting draws on both health MIS data and the social registry.
